results.name: Traditional Chinese Siheyuan Courtyard
results.description:
This is a detailed 3D model of a traditional Beijing Siheyuan, the iconic courtyard residence known for its classical Chinese architecture. A siheyuan is a type of dwelling commonly found throughout China, especially in Beijing and rural Shanxi. Throughout Chinese history, this layout was the foundational pattern for residences, palaces, temples, monasteries, family businesses, and government offices.

results.name: Small Chinese imperial style building
results.description:
A small yet elegant Chinese building inspired by the architecture of the Forbidden City. This structure features a hip-and-gable roof (歇山顶), traditional roof figures, reflecting the grandeur of imperial design in a compact form. 






Thanks to TRNKL for the exquisite roof figures of this model.

results.name: Humility Brings Prosperity gate - point cloud
results.description:
A big point cloud of the Humility Brings Prosperity gate, now installed in Gallery 200 at Mia.

*The gate comes from Shanxi province, which, because of its dry climate, contains the largest concentration of surviving historic wooden structures in China. An inscription on the main beam dates the gate to 1858, during the Qing dynasty (1644–1912).*

[More info](https://collections.artsmia.org/art/127331/humility-brings-prosperity-gate-china)

*This imposing gate once formed the entrance to the main courtyard of an urban middle-class family compound. The four-character panel over the doorway reads, Humility Brings Prosperity (Lüqian Jianfeng 履謙漸豐). The gate demonstrates the hallmarks of traditional Chinese architecture: a post-and-lintel structure that supports a graceful gable roof and intricate rafters, as well as brackets that extend the eaves and provide decoration. Like other works of traditional Chinese architecture, no glue or nails were used, and the gate was assembled using only joinery and wooden pins.*

results.name: Celadon jar with architecture and proto-Buddhas
results.description:
Dated 287 (Western Jin period). Excavated in 1983 from a tomb at the construction site of a steel factory in Hangzhou, China. Zhejiang Provincial Museum, Gushan Branch. </br>
This type of ceramicware, sometimes referred to as the "underground barns (*gucang*)" or "soul urns (*hunping*)," was frequently used as grave goods (*mingqi*) in 3rd-century tombs in cities along China's southeast coast.</br>
The cover of this jar is shaped into a building complex with a central tower, a courtyard enclosure, and multistory gateways with beast guardians as columns. Most notable is the row of seated figures--identified as proto-Buddhist icons--around the bottom of the cover; here we witness one of the earliest cases where Buddhist iconography intruded into indigenous Chinese art.</br>
(Note: images of the back of the jar are largely missing due to glares of the museum lighting on the protective glass case, which makes photographing difficult.)

results.name: Chiva Khyo1
results.description:
Chiva are monuments with archaeological, historical, social and economical values. They are spread all over Kathmandu valley in thousands. Promotion and preservation is the need of time. At a place called ChivaKhyo(in other words courtyard-open space with Chivas) in Kathmandu there is a large Chiva and many smaller Chivas around that established by general public. Beautiful place. This is a model of one of the smaller Chiva. For more information visit https://facebook.com/chivachaitya

results.name: Temple of Literature: Gate of Great Success
results.description:
The Fourth Courtyard: Gate of Great Success & Attained Talent Sanctuary
The fourth courtyard lies behind the Gate of Great Success, the central area, as well as the main architecture of the Temple of Literature. It consists of two large works arranged parallel and connected by other houses. This place is used for the worshiping of Confucius, four most brilliant students of Confucius (Mencius, Yanhui, Zengshen, and Zisi) and Ten Chinese Philosophers.

results.name: Contemporary Zen Chinese Courtyard
results.description:
Design Overview
This is an authentic private residence courtyard project located in Sichuan, China, featuring a three-dimensional zen landscape. The design comprises five functional zones:

Entrance Garden -  welcoming path
Side Garden - Open-air dining area for 6 people
Sunken Courtyard - Meditation and reading space 
Viewing Garden -  landscape artwork with water and plants
Rooftop Garden - Cloud-kissing aerial zen retreat

Modeling Software: SketchUp 2018 
Supported Formats: OBJ
